mkdir -p messy-repo && cd messy-repo

# Create scattered files
touch README temp.txt config.yml old.log
mkdir old_version
touch old_version/backup.zip old_version/readme.md

# Logs and data everywhere
mkdir logs data extra notes
touch logs/error.log logs/temp.log logs/debug.txt
touch data/data1.csv data/data2.csv
touch extra/todo.txt extra/.hiddenfile

# Confusing subfolders
mkdir -p bin bin_backup
touch bin/run.sh bin_backup/old_run.sh

# Unused nested dirs
mkdir -p temp/junk1 temp/junk2
touch temp/junk1/tmp1.log temp/junk2/tmp2.tmp

# Empty useless folders
mkdir unused_folder another_one

# Create deeply nested dirs
mkdir -p src/utils/old src/components/temp
touch src/main.js src/utils/helper.sh src/utils/old/legacy.sh
touch src/components/button.js src/components/temp/tmp.js

make
clean-repo/
├── README
├── config/
│   └── config.yml
├── logs/
│   └── error.log
├── scripts/
│   └── run.sh
├── src/
│   ├── main.js
│   ├── utils/
│   │   └── helper.sh
│   └── components/
│       └── button.js
├── data/
│   ├── data1.csv
│   └── data2.csv

tell comands

To reorganize your `messy-repo/` directory into a cleaner structure like `clean-repo/`, here's the set of shell commands you'd use:

```bash
# Step 1: Create clean-repo directory structure
mkdir -p clean-repo/config
mkdir -p clean-repo/logs
mkdir -p clean-repo/scripts
mkdir -p clean-repo/src/utils
mkdir -p clean-repo/src/components
mkdir -p clean-repo/data

# Step 2: Move the files into the appropriate folders
mv messy-repo/README clean-repo/
mv messy-repo/config.yml clean-repo/config/
mv messy-repo/logs/error.log clean-repo/logs/
mv messy-repo/bin/run.sh clean-repo/scripts/
mv messy-repo/src/main.js clean-repo/src/
mv messy-repo/src/utils/helper.sh clean-repo/src/utils/
mv messy-repo/src/components/button.js clean-repo/src/components/
mv messy-repo/data/data1.csv clean-repo/data/
mv messy-repo/data/data2.csv clean-repo/data/
```

### Optional: Clean up the original repo (if needed)
If you're confident and want to remove all the mess:
```bash
rm -rf messy-repo/
```

This keeps only the important files and folders and tosses junk like:
- `temp`, `extra`, `bin_backup`, `old_version`, `unused_folder`, etc.
- Hidden or irrelevant files (`.hiddenfile`, `.log`, `.tmp`, `readme.md` in wrong place)

Let me know if you want a script that does this cleanup in one go.
